[SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementarity as a combination of relevance and dissimilarity, using low-pass and mid-pass graph filters with attention to balance them. Useful principle: broad embedding similarity alone cannot represent functional complements. [MMSC (2025, revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22268) explicitly treats co-view/co-purchase associations as noisy weak supervision and learns relation-aware representations with denoising. However, it uses a multimodal foundation model and LLM-assisted supervision, so its implementation does not meet the no-pretrained-weights constraint.

Text-enhanced sequential recommendation exists, but the retrieved examples do not establish a directly matching from-scratch solution. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) encodes titles, descriptions and reviews with BERT; reviews and pretrained BERT are outside this task’s inputs. A plausible research adaptation—not a verified published recipe—is a small randomly initialized token encoder trained jointly with SASRec, combining ID and title/description embeddings through a learned gate. Separate candidate-conditioned relation heads could capture different predictive connections, but without relation labels these remain latent patterns, not demonstrated substitutes or complements. Train on next-item prediction, treat succession as uncertain association, avoid ownership-based redundancy penalties, and assess text fusion and relation heads through separate validation ablations.
